Baylor is moving forward with their plans to hire UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor as their next head coach. Word is being disseminated this evening to various college football reporters. Traylor is 63-28 in seven seasons at UTSA.

The program he took over had won seven games in the two seasons before he arrived.
He's 63-28 in seven seasons, with back-to-back Conference USA championships in 2021 and 2022, and he has never had a losing record as a college head coach. UTSA says he's 39-5 at home, including 29-1 against league opponents at the Alamodome.

Nothing has been signed yet, and Traylor still has a championship game to coach in the stadium where he built this program. If the deal is finalized in the coming days, the UTSA job will open too. Related: Baylor search reportedly "zeroing in" on UTSA's Jeff Traylor
It's UTSA's third 10-win season, all of them under Traylor, and the first time the program will host the American title game. When the job opened last month, FootballScoop had Traylor at the top of the list, and he was the personal pick in our coaching autopsy of Dave Aranda's tenure.
Traylor won three state championships at Gilmer High School in East Texas. He broke into college coaching on Charlie Strong's Texas staff in 2015, then worked for Chad Morris at SMU and Arkansas before UTSA named him head coach in December 2019. The program he took over had won seven games in the two seasons before he arrived.
